newsitem.title: USA: Toy Biz, Marvel creditors end plan.
newsitem.headline: Toy Biz, Marvel creditors end plan.

text.p: Toy Biz Inc said on Thursday that it and Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's bondholders committee have elected to terminate their joint proposal to bring the comic book publisher out of bankruptcy.
Toy Biz representatives declined to give a reason why the plan was terminated.

Toy Biz said in a statement it intends to continue to engage in discussions with the Marvel's bondholders committee and other parties in the Marvel Chapter 11 reorganization, but it would not make assurances that an agreement can be reached.
Toy Biz said it would not comment about any ongoing discussions or rumors about Marvel's reorganization.

A spokesman from Marvel's bondholders committee said "We do not know what Toy Biz is doing, as the company announced an agreement with us last week and now its Perelman-controlled board has rejected it without explanation."
Toy Biz's move to end this plan is the latest of a series of shaky alliances since November when Marvel first warned investors that it might go bankrupt.
Marvel's bondholders and Toy Biz announced a plan last week for combining the companies, giving 40 percent to Toy Biz shareholders and 60 percent owned by Marvel's shareholders.

Toy Biz is presently 27 percent owned by Marvel Entertainment. The proposed reorganization would cut financier Ronald Perelman's 80 percent stake before the bankruptcy to 13 percent through his holdings in Toy Biz.

Marvel's bondholders, led by Carl Icahn, wanted to sell off Marvel's trading cards and sticker businesses and raise cash from a rights offering to pay off Marvel's leading bank creditor Chase Manhattan Corp.
"We are proceeding with our own reorganization plan which is scheduled for a June 16 disclosure statement hearing before the bankruptcy court," the Marvel bondholder spokesman said.
"If Toy Biz wants to reopen discussions, once they've gotten their act together internally, we will consider it at that time," he added.
Perelman proposed a deal in November that would have diluted the common stock of Marvel by merging it with Toy Biz, but he would have retained 80 percent control of the merged companies.

Perelman's holding companies that control 80 percent of Marvel and Marvel filed Chapter 11 in December. The holding companies had nearly $900 million in bonds outstanding and the 80 percent stake in Marvel was used as collateral for the bonds.
Toy Biz representatives declined to say whether the board was unanimous in its support of backing out of the reorganization with Marvel's bondholders.
